forces.title: Significant power transmission capex planned under NEP
forces.description: India's power transmission sector is poised for substantial capital expenditure scale-up under the National Electricity Policy (NEP) 2022–32. This includes Rs 9.16 lakh crore (US$ 108.31 billion) total outlay by FY32, with Rs 6.60 lakh crore for Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) alone. This plan aims to add over 6.00 lakh ckm of transmission lines and 24.00 lakh MVA of transformation capacity, directly boosting demand for large power transformers, HVDC/FACTS systems, and HV switchgear.

forces.title: Persistent project execution challenges for transmission infrastructure
forces.description: Despite ambitious targets under NEP 2022–32, the power transmission sector faces recurring execution challenges. These include difficulties with right-of-way acquisition, delays in forest clearances, and land acquisition issues for substations. These hurdles have led to underachievement of transmission line addition targets in recent years and time overruns for many tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) projects, creating bottlenecks for Heavy Electrical Equipment suppliers.

forces.title: Data center expansion drives demand for power generation and grid equipment
forces.description: The rapid expansion of data centers, fueled by increasing demand for AI, IoT, and cloud storage, is creating significant electricity needs. This directly translates into strong demand for Heavy Electrical Equipment, specifically on-site and distributed power solutions like modular turbines and industrial generators. Furthermore, the rising electricity consumption from data centers boosts demand for grid technology, including large power transformers and HV switchgear, for grid modernization and new power generation capacity.

forces.title: Increased infrastructure spending and power sector focus
forces.description: Government's strong focus on infrastructure development, including railways, roads, urban infrastructure, and critically, the power sector, acts as a significant tailwind. Policy support for the engineering sector, including electrical machinery, alongside initiatives to facilitate private investment in infrastructure, directly drives demand for heavy electrical equipment required in power generation, transmission, and large-scale industrial applications. This sustained government emphasis provides a stable demand base for the sector.

forces.title: Favorable policies encourage investment and market growth
forces.description: The electrical machinery industry benefits from supportive policies such as de-licensing and 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) through the automatic route. These measures facilitate the entry of major global players like GE and ABB, enhancing competition and technological advancement. Government initiatives such as SEZs for the engineering sector and incentives for power generation capacity additions further stimulate demand and investment in Heavy Electrical Equipment, creating a conducive environment for sector growth.

forces.title: Inter-state transmission network expansion for renewable energy evacuation
forces.description: India's ambitious plans to invest US$ 34.2 billion by 2030 in setting up an inter-state transmission network (ISTS) are primarily driven by the need to evacuate renewable energy. This significant investment directly boosts the demand for high-voltage transmission equipment, including large power transformers, HVDC/FACTS systems, and HV switchgear, critical for integrating distributed and large-scale renewable generation into the national grid. This provides a clear, long-term growth avenue for Heavy Electrical Equipment manufacturers.

forces.title: Significant power generation capacity additions boost equipment demand
forces.description: India has seen substantial additions to its installed power generation capacity, with 52,536.49 MW added in FY26 (till Jan 2026), bringing the total to 5,20,511 MW. This growth, particularly in fossil-fuel and non-fossil fuel sources, directly drives the demand for power turbines (steam, gas, hydro) and large industrial generators, which are core components of Heavy Electrical Equipment. Furthermore, the planned expansion of the civil nuclear sector will further contribute to this demand.

forces.title: Geopolitical tensions and macroeconomic volatility pose risks
forces.description: Escalating geopolitical hostilities, particularly the West Asia crisis, introduce significant macroeconomic uncertainties. This includes elevated global energy prices, potential disruptions to trade routes, and increased fiscal pressures on governments. While the capital goods sector has shown strong sales growth, the moderating capital flows and potential for broader economic slowdown could impact overall investment appetite from utilities and large industrials, creating a cautious outlook for long-cycle Heavy Electrical Equipment projects.

forces.title: Moderation in state capital expenditure due to fiscal constraints
forces.description: State capital expenditure growth is projected to moderate to 8–10% in FY27, down from an estimated 17% in FY26. This slowdown is attributed to tighter fiscal headroom, lower growth in revenue receipts (especially from central transfers), and higher revenue expenditure commitments. As state utilities and large industrial projects often rely on state government funding or support, this moderation in capex could translate into reduced demand or slower project progression for certain Heavy Electrical Equipment orders.

viewpoints.title: Capital goods sector set for positive growth driven by strong order book
viewpoints.description: IBEF, citing ICRA, indicates a 'Positive' outlook for India's capital goods sector, projecting 13-15% annual growth over the next 2-3 years. This positive sentiment is underpinned by a record order book of Rs. 1.41 lakh crore (US$ 16.50 billion) as of September 2024, coupled with a substantial government capital expenditure allocation of Rs. 11.2 lakh crore (US$ 131.04 billion) for FY26. This outlook provides a strong tailwind for Heavy Electrical Equipment as a core component of capital goods.

viewpoints.title: Capital goods show strong sales growth amidst volatile macroeconomic environment
viewpoints.description: CareEdge reports that the capital goods sector demonstrated strong net sales growth in Q3 FY26 (above 16% and operating profits above 20%), indicating robust performance. However, this positive momentum is tempered by significant external headwinds, including escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, rising energy costs, and potential fiscal pressures. While domestic fundamentals for capital goods remain strong, the evolving global situation poses monitorable risks to the broader economic outlook, which could indirectly affect long-cycle projects.

market_sizing.methodology: The value represents the market size for heavy electrical equipment in India for the fiscal year 2025. This includes large-scale electrical equipment for utility and large industrial power generation, transmission, and HV control.

demand_drivers.description: Rising peak power demand and overall electricity consumption drive the need for new power generation capacity and associated generator sets.

market_sizing.methodology: The market size for generators in India for 2025. Forecasted to grow to US$ 2.14 billion by 2034. This includes large industrial generators and diesel generator sets, relevant for power generation applications.

demand_drivers.description: New power plants and expanded generation capabilities require more power transformers for grid integration.

demand_drivers.driver: Expansion of Transmission and Distribution Systems
demand_drivers.description: Modernization and growth of electricity networks necessitate investment in transmission-grade transformers to enhance grid stability and capacity.

market_sizing.methodology: The revenue generated by the India power transformer market in FY22, projected to reach US$ 3.4 billion by FY30. This refers to large power transformers (>100 MVA, transmission-grade) as included in the Heavy Electrical Equipment definition.

demand_drivers.description: Upgrading and expanding electricity grids to accommodate new generation sources and increasing load demand drives the need for high-voltage switchgear.
Large industrial facilities require robust switchgear for controlling and protecting heavy electrical loads.

market_sizing.methodology: The global market size for switchgear, projected to reach US$ 179.30 billion by 2034. This includes HV switchgear (>36kV) which is part of Heavy Electrical Equipment, necessary for high-voltage control in transmission systems. No India-specific split for HV switchgear is provided.

demand_drivers.description: Projected increase to 458 GW by FY32 from ~275 GW (mid FY25) necessitates grid expansion.
Target of 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030 requires substantial transmission infrastructure for evacuation.
Government policy outlines significant planned investments and capacity additions in the transmission sector.

market_sizing.methodology: India's National Electricity Policy (NEP) 2022–32 outlines a transmission expansion plan with a total capital outlay of Rs 9.16 lakh crore (US$ 108.31 billion) by FY32. Of this, Rs 6.60 lakh crore (US$ 78.02 billion) is for Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) and the balance for intra-state networks. The plan targets adding over 6.00 lakh circuit-kilometres (ckm) of transmission lines and more than 24.00 lakh MVA of transformation capacity by FY32. Average annual capex for transmission is projected at ~Rs 81,000 crore (US$ 9.58 billion) from FY26-FY31.

demand_drivers.description: Government-backed initiatives to triple nuclear power generation capacity drives demand for large power generation turbines and associated equipment.

market_sizing.methodology: India's installed nuclear power capacity reached 8,780 MW in November 2025 and is projected to increase to 22,480 MW by 2031 with the completion of ongoing and sanctioned projects. This capacity expansion necessitates demand for large-scale power generation equipment including steam turbines and generators.
